sources.title: Improved conversion, selectivity, and stability during CO2 methanation by the incorporation of Ce in Ni, Co, and Fe-hydrotalcite-derived catalysts

evidence.section: 3.2.3. Extent of the process: yield and stability of the best MMO
evidence.text_snippet:
Remarkably MMONiCo + Ce 
remained more stable than MMONiCo with no significant changes in 
catalytic activity (~85 % of CO2 conversion after 1400 min of contin-
uous use).

evidence.section: 3.2.3. Extent of the process: yield and stability of the best MMO
evidence.text_snippet: The SYT values followed the order MMONiCo + Ce (168 mol CH4 h−1 L−1) > MMONiCo (150 mol CH4 h−1 L−1) > MMONi + Ce (148 mol CH4 h−1 L−1) > MMONiFe + Ce (108 mol CH4 h−1 L−1) > OMNi (105 mol CH4 h−1 L−1) > MMONiFe (80 mol CH4 h−1 L−1).

evidence.section: 3.2.3. Extent of the process: yield and stability of the best MMO
evidence.text_snippet: Additionally, the MMONiCo + Ce material showed high stability, achieving elevated CO2 conversion (~85 %) even after 1400 min of continuous use.
